NYC: New York is the country's biggest Caribbean music market, from dancehall nights at S.O.B.'s and Brooklyn Bowl to arena headliners at Barclays Center, UBS Arena and the Kings Theatre in Flatbush. Live Reggae Music also covers Brooklyn Paramount, Irving Plaza, Terminal 5, Reggae Fest and weFETE soca parties, plus New Jersey rooms like the Prudential Center, NJPAC and the Starland Ballroom. Labor Day weekend brings the New York Carnival and West Indian Day Parade on Eastern Parkway.
PHL: Philadelphia's reggae, dancehall and afrobeats shows land at Union Transfer, Franklin Music Hall, The Fillmore in Fishtown, Underground Arts and World Cafe Live, with summer headliners at the Mann Center. Within 50 miles the list also takes in the Ardmore Music Hall on the Main Line and shows in Wilmington, Trenton and South Jersey.
BOS: Boston's reggae and Caribbean shows play Big Night Live by TD Garden, MGM Music Hall at Fenway, House of Blues, the Paradise and Brighton Music Hall, with smaller nights at The Sinclair in Cambridge. Roxbury, Dorchester and Mattapan host the city's Caribbean community, and Boston Carnival fills Franklin Park every summer.
BAL: Baltimore's reggae and dancehall shows play Rams Head Live, Baltimore Soundstage, the Ottobar and CFG Bank Arena, and the city's Caribbean Carnival runs every summer. Because Washington, D.C. is so close, many of the biggest Caribbean and African shows at The Anthem, Echostage and the Howard Theatre are also within 50 miles.
DC: Washington has one of the strongest African and Caribbean music scenes in the country. Afrobeats and amapiano headliners fill Echostage and Capital One Arena, and reggae plays the 9:30 Club, The Anthem, the Howard Theatre and Union Stage. The list also covers The Fillmore Silver Spring, MGM National Harbor and the DC Caribbean Carnival each June.
PIT: Pittsburgh's reggae and reggae-rock shows mostly play Mr. Smalls Theatre in Millvale, Stage AE, the Thunderbird Café and Crafthouse Stage & Grill. Touring bands like Steel Pulse, SOJA and Iration usually stop here on their eastern runs.
CLE: Cleveland's reggae shows play the House of Blues, the Beachland Ballroom in Collinwood, the Grog Shop in Cleveland Heights, Globe Iron and Jacobs Pavilion on the Flats. Within 50 miles the list also covers Akron and the rest of Northeast Ohio.
NSH: Nashville's reggae, reggae-rock and afrobeats shows play Brooklyn Bowl Nashville, The Basement East, Marathon Music Works and, for the biggest names, the Ryman Auditorium. Touring reggae-rock bands often route through here between Atlanta and the Midwest.
PWM: Portland, Maine is a regular stop for touring reggae and reggae-rock bands, which play the State Theatre, Port City Music Hall and Aura downtown. Live Reggae Music lists them alongside shows elsewhere in southern Maine and along the New Hampshire seacoast.
CHI: Chicago's Caribbean and African shows play the Concord Music Hall, House of Blues, Thalia Hall, Metro, the Aragon Ballroom and The Salt Shed, with the biggest afrobeats headliners at the United Center. The list also covers Evanston's SPACE, The Promontory in Hyde Park and the Chicago Caribbean Carnival each summer.
ATL: Atlanta is one of the biggest Caribbean and African music cities in the South. Shows play Center Stage, Variety Playhouse, Terminal West, The Tabernacle and the Coca-Cola Roxy, and arena headliners fill State Farm Arena and Gas South Arena. Atlanta Caribbean Carnival takes over the city every May.
RIC: Richmond's reggae and reggae-rock shows play The National, The Broadberry and The Camel. Touring bands moving between D.C. and the Carolinas stop here regularly, and the list also covers shows around Petersburg and Williamsburg.
ORF: Hampton Roads' reggae shows play The NorVa in downtown Norfolk and Elevation 27 and the Sandler Center in Virginia Beach. Summer brings reggae-rock tours to the oceanfront, and the list also covers Chesapeake, Hampton and Newport News.
HFD: Hartford's Caribbean community is one of the largest in New England, and the West Indian Independence Celebration fills the city every August. Shows play the Webster Theater and Infinity Hall, and the biggest names play Foxwoods and Mohegan Sun, both within 50 miles.
NHV: New Haven's reggae and dancehall shows play Toad's Place, College Street Music Hall and the Westville Music Bowl, and the list also covers the Webster Theater in Hartford. Many New York City-area acts make the trip up I-95, and Foxwoods and Mohegan Sun are within reach to the east.
MIA: South Florida's Caribbean music scene centers on Miami Gardens, Lauderhill and Little Haiti. Big shows play Hard Rock Live in Hollywood, Kaseya Center, Bayfront Park, The Fillmore Miami Beach and Revolution Live in Fort Lauderdale. Live Reggae Music also lists Best of the Best in May, Reggae Fest Miami, the Miami Broward Carnival each October and Wynwood's afrobeats nights.
TPA: Tampa Bay's reggae shows play Jannus Live and the Mahaffey Theater in St. Petersburg, The Ritz Ybor, Ruth Eckerd Hall and The BayCare Sound in Clearwater. Big arena shows land at the Yuengling Center. Every spring Reggae Rise Up Florida brings a weekend of reggae to Vinoy Park.
ORL: Orlando's reggae and Caribbean shows play Hard Rock Live, the House of Blues at Disney Springs, The Vanguard and The Beacham. The list also covers Sanford, Cocoa Village and the Space Coast, plus the Orlando Carnival each spring.
CIN: Cincinnati's reggae and reggae-rock shows play the MegaCorp Pavilion across the river in Newport, Kentucky, Bogart's in Corryville and Madison Live in Covington. Within 50 miles the list also covers shows in Dayton.
STL: St. Louis's reggae shows play The Pageant and Delmar Hall on the Delmar Loop, the Old Rock House, Atomic Garage and the Duck Room at Blueberry Hill. Touring reggae-rock bands stop here on most Midwest runs.
MSP: The Twin Cities' reggae and afrobeats shows play First Avenue, the Fine Line, the Varsity Theater and the Cabooze. Minneapolis–St. Paul has one of the largest East African communities in the country, so African headliners stop here often.
MKE: Milwaukee's reggae shows play Turner Hall Ballroom, the Pabst Theater, Shank Hall and The Rave/Eagles Club. Chicago's bigger rooms are about 90 miles away, so the list sticks to southeastern Wisconsin.
DET: Detroit's reggae and Caribbean shows play Saint Andrew's Hall, The Majestic, The Fillmore and The Magic Bag in Ferndale, and the biggest African headliners play Little Caesars Arena. The list also covers the Detroit Caribbean Cultural Festival and suburban shows in Belleville and Pontiac.
DEN: Denver is one of the strongest reggae towns in the West. Cervantes' Masterpiece Ballroom books reggae and dub regularly, and the Ogden Theatre, Mission Ballroom and Fillmore Auditorium host touring headliners. In spring and summer, Red Rocks Amphitheatre has some of the year's biggest reggae nights.
IND: Indianapolis's reggae shows play The Vogue in Broad Ripple, Old National Centre downtown and the Hi-Fi in Fountain Square. Touring reggae-rock bands stop here between Chicago, Cincinnati and Louisville.
AUS: Austin's reggae shows play Stubb's, Emo's, Mohawk and the Moody Center. The long-running Austin Reggae Festival returns every April, and the list also covers San Marcos and Round Rock.
DFW: Dallas–Fort Worth's reggae, dancehall and afrobeats shows play House of Blues Dallas, The Echo Lounge, Ferris Wheelers and The Pavilion at Toyota Music Factory in Irving. Afrobeats tours stop here often, and the area also has a summer Caribbean carnival.
PHX: Phoenix's reggae shows play the Marquee Theatre in Tempe, The Van Buren, Crescent Ballroom, the Arizona Financial Theatre and Talking Stick Resort Amphitheatre. Every spring Reggae Rise Up Arizona brings a weekend of reggae to the Valley.
LAS: Las Vegas books reggae all year at the House of Blues, Brooklyn Bowl Las Vegas and The Theater at Virgin, with afrobeats and dancehall headliners at Strip resorts like the Fontainebleau. Reggae in the Desert brings a festival weekend every spring.
LA: Los Angeles and Orange County have one of the country's busiest reggae scenes. Dub Club holds its weekly night at the Echoplex, and touring acts play The Belasco, The Novo, the Hollywood Palladium, The Wiltern, the Kia Forum and YouTube Theater. The list also covers The Observatory in Santa Ana, House of Blues Anaheim, Cali Vibes in Long Beach and BeachLife in Redondo Beach.
SFO: The Bay Area's reggae shows play The Independent, The Fillmore and The Regency Ballroom in San Francisco, the Fox Theater in Oakland, the UC Theatre and Cornerstone in Berkeley, and The Ritz in San Jose. Big African headliners play Chase Center, and Santa Cruz shows have their own page.
SEA: Seattle's reggae shows play the Showbox, Showbox SoDo, the Neptune, The Crocodile and the Paramount Theatre, and Nectar Lounge in Fremont books reggae and dub regularly. Summer brings outdoor shows at Marymoor Park in Redmond, and the list also covers Tacoma.
HOU: Houston has big Nigerian and Caribbean communities, and its shows play the House of Blues, 713 Music Hall, Bayou Music Center and White Oak Music Hall. Arena headliners fill the Toyota Center, and every summer brings the Houston Caribbean Festival.
SAN: San Diego is a reggae-rock capital. Belly Up in Solana Beach, the Music Box, Observatory North Park and House of Blues all book reggae regularly, and Humphreys by the Bay hosts summer shows on Shelter Island. The list also covers The Sound in Del Mar, Viejas Arena and Oceanside.
HNL: Island reggae plays in Honolulu all year. Blue Note Hawaii, Hawaiian Brian's and The Republik book local and touring acts, and big shows fill the Waikiki Shell and the Neal S. Blaisdell Arena. Expect Hawaiian favorites like J Boog, Common Kings, HIRIE and Kolohe Kai alongside touring bands from the mainland and Jamaica.
PDX: Portland's reggae shows play the Crystal Ballroom, the Roseland Theater, Revolution Hall, the Star Theater, the Aladdin Theater and Mississippi Studios, with dancehall and afrobeats nights at clubs like The Get Down. The list also covers Vancouver, Washington, and the west-side suburbs.
SAC: Sacramento's reggae shows play Ace of Spades, Channel 24, Harlow's and the Memorial Auditorium, with big touring acts at Golden 1 Center and Hard Rock Live in Wheatland. The list also covers the Thunder Valley Casino Resort in Lincoln and shows in Davis and Roseville.
SCZ: Santa Cruz has been a reggae town for decades. Moe's Alley books roots reggae, dub and dancehall regularly, and touring bands also play The Catalyst, the Rio Theatre and the Felton Music Hall. The list also covers the Monterey Peninsula, including the Golden State Theatre.
SBA: Santa Barbara and Ventura County are a reggae stronghold on the Central Coast. Shows play the Majestic Ventura Theater and Ventura Music Hall, the Santa Barbara Bowl, the Arlington Theatre and SOhO Music Club, and the Libbey Bowl in Ojai. Reggae-rock bands like Rebelution got their start here.
OGG: Maui's biggest reggae shows play the Maui Arts & Cultural Center in Kahului, at the outdoor A&B Amphitheater or the Castle Theater. Touring acts like Steel Pulse, SOJA, The Green and Katchafire make the trip, alongside Hawaiian reggae favorites.
SLC: Salt Lake City is a regular stop on western reggae tours. Shows play The Depot, The Complex, The Union Event Center, the Commonwealth Room and Metro Music Hall. In summer, outdoor shows move to Red Butte Garden, the Utah First Credit Union Amphitheatre and Canyons Village in Park City.
CMH: Columbus's reggae and afrobeats shows play the Newport Music Hall on campus, KEMBA Live!, The Bluestone and A&R Music Bar, with arena headliners at Nationwide Arena. Central Ohio's large West and East African communities bring African music tours here too.
MCI: Kansas City's reggae shows play the Uptown Theater and recordBar in Westport, The Truman, Knuckleheads, and Liberty Hall and The Granada in Lawrence. Summer amphitheater tours stop at Azura Amphitheater in Bonner Springs and Starlight Theatre.
CLT: Charlotte's Caribbean and African communities have grown quickly. Shows play The Fillmore Charlotte and The Underground at the AvidXchange Music Factory, the Neighborhood Theatre in NoDa and the Spectrum Center. Summer tours play Truliant Amphitheater (formerly PNC Music Pavilion) and Skyla Credit Union Amphitheatre.
RDU: The Triangle's reggae shows play the Lincoln Theatre and The Ritz in Raleigh, Cat's Cradle in Carrboro, and Motorco Music Hall and DPAC in Durham. Summer tours play the Koka Booth Amphitheatre in Cary and Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek.
JAX: Jacksonville's reggae and reggae-rock shows play the Ponte Vedra Concert Hall, the Florida Theatre, Daily's Place and Jack Rabbits in San Marco, with summer nights out at Jacksonville Beach. The list also covers St. Augustine, including the St. Augustine Amphitheatre.
PBI: Palm Beach County has a large Jamaican and Haitian community. Shows play the iTHINK Financial Amphitheatre and the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach, Respectable Street downtown, and the Sunset Cove Amphitheater and Mizner Park in Boca Raton, where Reggae Rise Up's Holidaze festival takes place. The list also reaches north to Jupiter and Port St. Lucie.
SAT: San Antonio's reggae shows play the Aztec Theatre, The Espee, Paper Tiger and the Boeing Center at Tech Port, with arena headliners at the Frost Bank Center. The list also covers New Braunfels and San Marcos, so many Austin-bound tours show up here too.
